intertidal_analysis_short

tena

1 Overview

This document:

  • Loads and merges pH/TA/nutrients and fDOM datasets
  • Cleans data and applies outlier handling (IQR rule)
  • Summarizes by habitat and diel period
  • Creates PCA for seasonal drivers
  • Plots relationships between variables to visualize processes
  • Visualizes diel and habitat patterns (boxplots)

2.1 Paths & Parameters

keep_times <- params$keep_times
control_label <- params$control_label

3 Data Loading & Merging

This section loads both fDOM and pH/nutrients CSVs, parses dates, and joins on shared identifiers. We keep all samples, regardless of missing data (full_join).

load_ok <- TRUE
tryCatch({
  data_ph <- read_csv(here::here("Data","Biogeochemistry","pHProbe_Data_calculated.csv"), na = c("NA", ""), show_col_types = FALSE) 
    #mutate(Sampling_Date = lubridate::mdy(Sampling_Date))
  data_fdom <- read_csv(here::here("Data","Biogeochemistry","fDOM_clean.csv"), na = c("NA", ""), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(Sampling_Date = lubridate::mdy(Sampling_Date))
  data_tidal <- read.csv(here::here("Data","tidal_exchange.csv")) %>%
    mutate(Sampling_Date = lubridate::mdy(Sampling_Date))

  data_merged <- full_join(
    data_ph,
    data_fdom,
    by = c("UniqueID", "Benthos", "Quad_ID", "Day_Night", "Sampling_Date", "Sampling_Time","Season")
  ) %>%
    mutate(Humic = UVHumic+VisibleHumic+MarineHumic,# make a column for humics
           Prot = Tryptophan+Tyrosine, # make a column for proteinaceaus fDOM
           NOx = NO3+NO2 # make a column of total N
           )
  data_merged <- data_merged %>%
    left_join(data_tidal, by = c("Sampling_Date", "Day_Night"))
  
  cat("Data loaded and merged successfully.\n")
  cat("Total merged samples:", nrow(data_merged), "\n")
}, error = function(e){
  load_ok <<- FALSE
  message("Error loading or merging files. Please check file paths and names.")
  message(e)
})

4 Cleaning & Pre-processing

We declare variable sets for identifiers, water chemistry, nutrients, and fDOM components. We retain only Dawn and Dusk samples, coerce numeric columns, set factor orders, drop NA grouping levels, and apply the 1.5×IQR rule as a conservative outlier filter (replacing outliers with NA).

# Identifier variables
id_vars <- c("UniqueID", "Season", "Benthos", "Quad_ID", "Day_Night", "Sampling_Date", "Tide")

# Water chemistry variables (from pH probe file)
water_chem_vars <- c("Salinity", "pH", "TempInSitu", "TA")

# Nutrient variables (from pH probe file)
nutrient_vars <- c("NO3", "PO4", "SIL", "NO2", "NH4", "NOx")

# fDOM variables (from fDOM file)
#fdom_vars <- c("UVHumic", "Tyrosine", "VisibleHumic", "MarineHumic",
#               "Tryptophan", "FulvicAcid", "BIX", "HIX", "FI", "M_to_C")

# reduced variables
fdom_vars <- c("Humic","Prot", "BIX", "HIX", "M_to_C")

all_numeric_vars <- c(water_chem_vars, nutrient_vars, fdom_vars)

# only vars of interest
numeric_vars <- c("pH", "TA", "NOx", "Humic", "Prot", "BIX", "HIX", "M_to_C")

ratio_vars <- c("pH", "TA", "NOx", "NH4", "BIX", "HIX")
  
raw_vars <- c("pH", "TA", "NOx", "Humic", "Prot")

# Helper to IQR-filter a numeric vector (returning NA for outliers)
iqr_filter <- function(x){
  if(!is.numeric(x)) return(x)
  q1 <- quantile(x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
  q3 <- quantile(x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
  iqr <- q3 - q1
  lo <- q1 - 1.5 * iqr
  hi <- q3 + 1.5 * iqr
  ifelse(x < lo | x > hi, NA_real_, x)
}

# Cleaned dataset
data_clean <- data_merged %>%
  filter(Day_Night %in% keep_times) %>%
  select(-M_to_C) %>%
  mutate(M_to_C = MarineHumic / VisibleHumic) %>%
  select(all_of(id_vars), any_of(all_numeric_vars)) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(all_numeric_vars), as.numeric)) %>%
  mutate(
    Benthos   = factor(Benthos, levels = c(control_label, "Rockweed", "Surfgrass", "Barnacle", "Mussel")),
    Day_Night = factor(Day_Night, levels = c("Dawn", "Dusk"))
  ) %>%
  drop_na(Benthos, Day_Night) %>%
  
  mutate(across(all_of(all_numeric_vars), iqr_filter))

5 Summary Statistics

Per habitat × diel period (and Season), we compute mean, SD, and sample size for all numeric variables.

data_summary <- data_clean %>%
  group_by(Benthos, Day_Night, Season) %>%
  summarise(
    across(all_of(all_numeric_vars), list(mean = ~ mean(., na.rm = TRUE),
                                          sd   = ~ sd(., na.rm = TRUE),
                                          n    = ~ sum(!is.na(.))
    )),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

6 Background plots

6.1 Correlation Matrix

We compute a Pearson correlation matrix on complete cases and visualize it with significance masking.

cor_data <- data_clean %>% select(all_of(ratio_vars)) %>% drop_na()

colnames(cor_data) <- gsub("M_to_C", "M :C", colnames(cor_data)) # fix m:c format

if(nrow(cor_data) > 0){
  cor_mat <- rstatix::cor_mat(cor_data)
  cor_p   <- rstatix::cor_pmat(cor_data)

  ggcorrplot(
    cor_mat,
    hc.order = TRUE,
    type = "lower",
    p.mat = cor_p,
    sig.level = 0.05,
    insig = "blank",
    lab = TRUE,
    lab_size = 2.5,
    colors = c("#6D9EC1", "white", "#E46726")
  )
} else {
  cat("Not enough complete data (after drop_na) to compute correlation matrix or PCA.\n")
}

6.2 PCA plots

6.2.1 Seasonal differences - PCA

Do different seasons have distinct chemical/fDOM signatures? Which variables drive those differences?

6.2.2 One PCA standardized within season

pca_biplot <- function(df,
                       vars,
                       season_var = "Season",
                       color_var = "Day_Night",
                       ellipse_var = "Benthos") {

  # select vars of interest
  df_sub <- df %>%
    select(all_of(c(vars, season_var, color_var, ellipse_var))) %>%
    drop_na(all_of(vars))

  # standardize within season
  df_scaled <- df_sub %>%
    group_by(.data[[season_var]]) %>%
    mutate(across(all_of(vars), scale)) %>%
    ungroup()

  # run PCA
  num_mat <- df_scaled %>%
    select(all_of(vars)) %>%
    as.matrix()

  pca_res <- prcomp(num_mat, scale. = FALSE)

  # get scores
  scores <- as.data.frame(pca_res$x[, 1:2])
  colnames(scores) <- c("PC1", "PC2")

  scores <- scores %>%
    bind_cols(
      df_scaled %>%
        select(all_of(c(season_var, color_var, ellipse_var)))
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      Day_Night = factor(Day_Night, levels = c("Dawn", "Dusk"))
    )

  # get loadings
  loadings <- as.data.frame(pca_res$rotation[, 1:2])
  colnames(loadings) <- c("PC1", "PC2")
  loadings$var <- rownames(loadings)

  # scale loadings
  mult <- min(
    diff(range(scores$PC1)) / diff(range(loadings$PC1)),
    diff(range(scores$PC2)) / diff(range(loadings$PC2))
  ) * 0.7

  loadings <- loadings %>%
    mutate(
      PC1 = PC1 * mult,
      PC2 = PC2 * mult
    )

  # variance
  var_expl <- (pca_res$sdev^2 / sum(pca_res$sdev^2)) * 100

  # make plot
  ggplot(scores, aes(PC1, PC2)) +

    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +

    geom_point(
      aes(color = Day_Night, shape = Day_Night),
      size = 3,
      alpha = 0.8
    ) +

    scale_color_manual(
      values = c(
        "Dawn" = "#FDB813",
        "Dusk" = "#003865"
      ),
      name = "Sampling Time"
    ) +

    scale_shape_manual(
      values = c(
        "Dawn" = 16,
        "Dusk" = 17
      ),
      name = "Sampling Time"
    ) +

    ggnewscale::new_scale_color() +

    stat_ellipse(
      aes(
        group = .data[[ellipse_var]],
        color = .data[[ellipse_var]]
      ),
      linewidth = 1,
      alpha = 0.8
    ) +

    scale_color_paletteer_d("nationalparkcolors::Acadia",
                            name = "Benthos") +

    geom_segment(
      data = loadings,
      aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = PC1, yend = PC2),
      arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm")),
      inherit.aes = FALSE
    ) +

    geom_text_repel(
      data = loadings,
      aes(PC1, PC2, label = var),
      size = 4,
      inherit.aes = FALSE
    ) +

    facet_wrap(as.formula(paste("~", season_var))) +

    labs(
      x = paste0("PC1 (", round(var_expl[1], 1), "%)"),
      y = paste0("PC2 (", round(var_expl[2], 1), "%)")
    ) +

    theme_bw()
}

# colored by benthos - no clear separation
pca_biplot(data_clean,
  vars      = ratio_vars,
  season_var = "Season",
  color_var = "Day_Night",
  ellipse_var = "Benthos")

# colored by dawn/dusk cleaner
pca_biplot(data_clean,
  vars      = ratio_vars,
  season_var = "Season",
  color_var = "Day_Night",
  ellipse_var = "Day_Night")

6.2.3 One PCA per season - shows pH decoupling from NOX, but I think the above one is better

pca_miplot_separate <- function(df,
                                vars,
                                season_var = "Season",
                                color_var = "Day_Night",
                                shape_var = "Day_Night",
                                ellipse_var = "Benthos") {

  
  # select data
  df_sub <- df %>%
    select(all_of(c(vars, season_var, color_var, shape_var, ellipse_var))) %>%
    drop_na(all_of(vars))
  
  # ---- 2. Initialize lists ----
  scores_list <- list()
  loadings_list <- list()
  
  # loop over seasons
  for(season in unique(df_sub[[season_var]])) {
    
    df_season <- df_sub %>% filter(.data[[season_var]] == season)
    
    # PCA per season
    pca <- prcomp(df_season[,vars], scale.=TRUE)
    
    # Scores
    sco <- as.data.frame(pca$x[,1:2])
    colnames(sco) <- c("PC1","PC2")
    sco <- cbind(sco, df_season[,c(season_var, color_var, ellipse_var)])
    
    # Loadings scaled to score space
    loadings <- as.data.frame(pca$rotation[,1:2])
    colnames(loadings) <- c("PC1","PC2")
    loadings$var <- rownames(loadings)
    
    # Scale arrows
    mult <- min(
      diff(range(sco$PC1)) / diff(range(loadings$PC1)),
      diff(range(sco$PC2)) / diff(range(loadings$PC2))
    ) * 0.7
    loadings$PC1 <- loadings$PC1 * mult
    loadings$PC2 <- loadings$PC2 * mult
    loadings[[season_var]] <- season
    
    # % variance explained for axis labels
    var_expl <- round(pca$sdev^2 / sum(pca$sdev^2) * 100, 1)
    sco$PC1_label <- paste0("PC1 (", var_expl[1], "%)")
    sco$PC2_label <- paste0("PC2 (", var_expl[2], "%)")
    
    # Store
    scores_list[[season]] <- sco
    loadings_list[[season]] <- loadings
  }
  
  # combine seasons
  scores_all <- bind_rows(scores_list)
  loadings_all <- bind_rows(loadings_list)
  
  # create plot
  ggplot(scores_all, aes(PC1, PC2)) +
    
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype="dashed") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype="dashed") +
    
    # Points: Day/Night
    geom_point(aes(color = .data[[color_var]], shape = .data[[shape_var]]),
               size=3, alpha=0.8) +
    scale_color_manual(values=c("Dawn"="#FDB813","Dusk"="#003865"),
                       name="Sampling Time") +
    scale_shape_manual(values=c(16,17), name="Sampling Time") +
    
    ggnewscale::new_scale_color() +
    
    # Ellipses by Benthos
    stat_ellipse(aes(group=.data[[ellipse_var]], color=.data[[ellipse_var]]),
                 linewidth=1, alpha=0.8) +
    scale_color_brewer(palette="Set2", name="Benthos") +
    
    # Loadings
    geom_segment(data=loadings_all, aes(x=0, y=0, xend=PC1, yend=PC2),
                 arrow=arrow(length=unit(0.2,"cm")), inherit.aes=FALSE) +
    geom_text_repel(data=loadings_all, aes(x=PC1, y=PC2, label=var),
                    size=4, segment.color="grey50", inherit.aes=FALSE) +
    
    # Facet by season
    facet_wrap(as.formula(paste("~", season_var))) +
    
    # Axis labels with % variance
    labs(
      x = unique(scores_all$PC1_label),
      y = unique(scores_all$PC2_label)
    ) +
    
    theme_bw()
}


pca_miplot_separate(data_clean,
  vars      = ratio_vars,
  season_var = "Season",
  color_var = "Day_Night",
  shape_var = "Day_Night",
  ellipse_var = "Benthos")

7.2 NH4 and NOx - “Microbial processes vary by benthos”

7.2.1 Original plot

ggplot(data_clean %>% 
         mutate(Benthos = factor(Benthos, levels = c("Open Ocean", "Barnacle", "Mussel", "Rockweed", "Surfgrass"))), 
       aes(x = NH4, y = NOx, color = Day_Night)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +   
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Dawn" = "#FDB813", "Dusk" = "#003865")) + 
  facet_grid2(Season~Benthos, scales = "free", switch = "y" ) + 
  labs( x = expression(paste("NH"[4]," (", mu, "mol L"^-1,")")), 
        y = expression(paste("NO"[x]," (", mu, "mol L"^-1,")")), 
        color = "Sampling Time" )

7.2.2 Within each benthos x season x sampling time, is there a relationship?

Strong mussel coupling in fall throughout the day = strong remineralization and nitrification.
Rockweeds at dawn = microbial processing at night, masked by NH4 uptake during the day.
Surfgrass at dusk
Barnacles only ones in Spring + only at dusk.

# ONLY KEEPING SIG LINES
## create log columns
data_logged <- data_clean %>%
  mutate(
    logNH4 = log(NH4),
    logNOx = log(NOx)
  )
## regression of nitrogens
nitrogenmodel <- lm(logNOx ~ logNH4 * Day_Night * Season * Benthos,
  data = data_logged
)
Anova(nitrogenmodel, type = "III")
## Anova Table (Type III tests)
## 
## Response: logNOx

## filter sig slopes
alpha <- 0.05

sig_slopes <- emm %>%
  filter(p.value < alpha) %>%
  transmute(
    Day_Night, Benthos, Season,
    slope = `logNH4.trend`
  )

## intercept on log scale for each panel at log(NH4)=0
new0 <- data_logged %>%
  distinct(Day_Night, Benthos, Season) %>%
  mutate(logNH4 = 0)

new0$intercept <- predict(nitrogenmodel, newdata = new0)

line_df <- new0 %>%
  left_join(sig_slopes, by = c("Day_Night", "Benthos", "Season")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(slope))

## plot
ggplot(data_logged %>%
    mutate(Benthos = factor(Benthos, levels = c("Open Ocean", "Barnacle", "Mussel", "Rockweed", "Surfgrass"))),
  aes(x = logNH4, y = logNOx, color = Day_Night)
) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_abline(
    data = line_df,
    aes(intercept = intercept, slope = slope, color = Day_Night),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Dawn" = "#FDB813", "Dusk" = "#003865")) +
  facet_grid2(Season ~ Benthos, 
              scales = "free", 
              switch = "y") +
  labs(
    x = expression(paste("log(NH"[4], ") (", mu, "mol L"^-1, ")")),
    y = expression(paste("log(NO"[x], ") (", mu, "mol L"^-1, ")")),
    color = "Sampling Time"
  )

There is a strong relationship between pH and HIX that interacts with season, but not different across benthos.

7.3.1 Only significant lines.

Only Open Ocean

# start by fitting the model to see significant trends
pHHIXmodel <- lm(HIX ~ pH * Season * Benthos, data = data_clean)
Anova(pHHIXmodel, type = "III")
## Anova Table (Type III tests)
## 
## Response: HIX
##                   Sum Sq  Df F value    Pr(>F)    
## (Intercept)        5.108   1 12.8764 0.0004572 ***
## pH                 4.589   1 11.5689 0.0008713 ***
## Season             8.534   1 21.5109 7.908e-06 ***
## Benthos            0.515   4  0.3244 0.8612628    
## pH:Season          8.596   1 21.6686 7.364e-06 ***
## pH:Benthos         0.530   4  0.3338 0.8548794    
## Season:Benthos     0.886   4  0.5583 0.6932595    
## pH:Season:Benthos  0.878   4  0.5532 0.6969741    
## Residuals         56.333 142                      
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
# only filter out significant slopes
alpha <- 0.05

tr_SB <- summary(emtrends(pHHIXmodel, 
                          specs = ~ Season * Benthos, 
                          var = "pH"),
                infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)) %>% # get p values
        as.data.frame()

print(tr_SB)

##  Spring Mussel     -0.140188 1.0319379 142 -2.180134  1.899758  -0.136  0.8921
## 
## Confidence level used: 0.95
sig_tr_SB <- tr_SB %>%
  filter(p.value < alpha) %>%
  transmute(
    Season,
    Benthos,
    slope = pH.trend
  )


# get intercepts
intercepts <- data_clean %>%
  distinct(Season, Benthos) %>%
  mutate(pH = 0)

intercepts$intercept <- predict(pHHIXmodel, newdata = intercepts)

line_df <- intercepts %>%
  left_join(sig_tr_SB, by = c("Season", "Benthos")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(slope))   # ONLY significant regressions

# plot sig lines
ggplot(
  data_clean,
  aes(x = pH, y = HIX, color = Benthos)
) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Open Ocean" = "#8C8C8C",
    "Surfgrass"  = "#5BB360",
    "Rockweed"   = "#5A8F5D",
    "Barnacle"   = "#6E86C2",
    "Mussel"     = "#233B75"
  )) +
  geom_abline(
    data = line_df,
    aes(intercept = intercept, slope = slope,
        color = Benthos),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  labs(
    x = expression(paste("pH")),
    y = expression(paste("HIX")),
    color = "Benthos"
  ) +
  facet_grid2(
    rows = vars(Season),
    cols = vars(Benthos),
    switch = "y"
  )

7.3.2 Drop benthos since it is not significantly different

They do look more different from each other during Spring. With Barnacles and mussels more similar than OO/rockweed and surfgrass in the middle.

# lines colored by benthos

TA decreases as pH increases in spring in barnacle and mussel plots. Surfgrass plots in fall = CCA?

# model
TAmodel <- lm(TA ~ pH * Benthos * Season, data = data_clean)
anova(TAmodel)
## Analysis of Variance Table
## 
## Response: TA
##                    Df Sum Sq Mean Sq F value    Pr(>F)    
## pH                  1   2607  2606.8 10.8279  0.001212 ** 
## Benthos             4   6382  1595.5  6.6274 5.506e-05 ***
## Season              1  10588 10588.4 43.9813 4.074e-10 ***
## pH:Benthos          4   2786   696.5  2.8929  0.023738 *

## Residuals         173  41649   240.7                      
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
# plot significant lines
alpha <- 0.05

TA_slopes <- summary(emtrends(TAmodel, 
                          specs = ~ Season * Benthos, 
                          var = "pH"),
                infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)) %>% # get p values
                as.data.frame()

print(TA_slopes)

## Confidence level used: 0.95
sig_TA_slopes <- TA_slopes %>%
  filter(p.value < alpha) %>%
  transmute(
    Season,
    Benthos,
    slope = pH.trend
  )

# get intercepts
intercepts <- data_clean %>%
  distinct(Season, Benthos) %>%
  mutate(pH = 0)

intercepts$intercept <- predict(TAmodel, newdata = intercepts)

line_df <- intercepts %>%
  left_join(sig_TA_slopes, by = c("Season", "Benthos")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(slope))   # ONLY significant regressions

# plot sig lines
ggplot(
  data_clean %>%
    mutate(Day_Night = factor(Day_Night, levels = c("Dusk", "Dawn"))),

8 Dawn vs Dusk analyses across Benthos and Seasons

Start by assessing assumptions of normality and homogeneity of variance.

# create long format df
testing_df <- data_clean %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(numeric_vars),
               names_to = "variable", values_to = "Value")

nutrient_vars <- c("NO3", "PO4", "SIL", "NO2", "NH4", "NOx")

# running lm and creating diagnostic plots
map_dfr(numeric_vars, function(v){
  df_sub <- testing_df %>%
    filter(variable == v) # filter by variable
    options(contrasts = c("contr.sum", "contr.poly"))
    fit <- lm(Value ~ Day_Night * Benthos * Season, data = df_sub)
  par(mfrow = c(2,2)) # create 2x2 for plots
  plot(fit, main = paste("Diagnostics for", v)) # check assumptions using qq and residuals plots
})
## # A tibble: 0 × 0
# NOx, Humic, Prot, HIX looks like they need to be transformed
transform_var <- c("NOx", "Humic", "Prot", "HIX")
transformed_var <- map_dfr(transform_var, function(v){
  testing_df %>%
    filter(variable == v) %>% # filter by variable
    mutate(Value = sqrt(Value),
           variable = paste0(v,"_transformed"))
})

# check that transformations worked
transformed_vars <- c("NOx_transformed", "Humic_transformed", "Prot_transformed", "HIX_transformed")
map_dfr(transformed_vars, function(v){
  df_sub <- transformed_var %>%
    filter(variable == v) # filter by variable
    options(contrasts = c("contr.sum", "contr.poly"))
    fit <- lm(Value ~ Day_Night * Benthos * Season, data = df_sub)
  par(mfrow = c(2,2)) # create 2x2 for plots
  plot(fit, main = paste("Diagnostics for", v)) # check assumptions using qq and residuals plots
})
## # A tibble: 0 × 0

8.1 ANOVA results

testing_df_norm <- bind_rows(testing_df, transformed_var) 
numeric_vars_normal <- c("pH", "TA", "NOx_transformed", "Humic_transformed", "Prot_transformed", "BIX", "HIX_transformed", "M_to_C")

# let's see all ANOVA results together
anovas_full <- map_dfr(numeric_vars_normal, function(v){
  df_sub <- testing_df_norm %>%
    filter(variable == v) # filter by variable
    options(contrasts = c("contr.sum", "contr.poly"))
    fit <- lmer(Value ~ Day_Night * Benthos * Season + (1| Quad_ID), data = df_sub)
    Anova(fit, type = "III") %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    rownames_to_column("term") %>%
    filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
    filter(`Pr(>Chisq)` < 0.05) %>% # see what's significant
    mutate(variable = v)
})
anovas_full %>%
  kable()

8.3 Diel boxplots with significance levels

build_sig_df <- function(var_name = ratio_vars, data = data_clean) {
  stopifnot(var_name %in% names(data))
  
  # fit ANOVA
  fml <- as.formula(paste(var_name, "~ Day_Night * Season * Benthos + (1|Quad_ID)"))
  fit <- lmer(fml, data = data)
  
  # Dawn vs Dusk within each Season × Benthos
  emm  <- emmeans(fit, ~ Day_Night | Season * Benthos)
  contr_df <- as.data.frame(contrast(emm, method = "revpairwise"))
  # columns: Season, Benthos, contrast, estimate, SE, df, t.ratio, p.value
  
  # Turn p-values into stars
  sig_df <- contr_df %>%
    select(Season, Benthos, p.value) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    mutate(sig = case_when(
      p.value < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p.value < 0.01  ~ "**",
      p.value < 0.05  ~ "*",
      TRUE            ~ "ns"
    )) %>%
    left_join(
      data %>%
        group_by(Season, Benthos) %>%
        summarise(y_pos = max(.data[[var_name]], na.rm = TRUE),
                  .groups = "drop"),
      by = c("Season", "Benthos")
    ) %>%
    mutate(y_pos = y_pos * 1.05) %>% # a bit above top whisker
    filter(sig != "ns")
}

plot_diel_with_sig <- function(var_name, var_label, 
                               data = data_clean,
                               free_y = FALSE) {
  stopifnot(var_name %in% names(data))
  
  sig_df <- build_sig_df(var_name, data = data)
  
  facet_scales <- if (free_y) "free_y" else "fixed"
  
  ggplot(
    data %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[var_name]])),
    aes(x = Day_Night, y = .data[[var_name]], fill = Day_Night)
  ) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
    geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.5, size = 2) +
    facet_grid(rows = vars(Season),cols = vars(Benthos),
              scales = facet_scales,switch = "y"
) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Dawn" = "#FDB813", "Dusk" = "#003865")) +
    labs(
      #title = paste("Diel Patterns in", var_label),
      x = "Sampling Time",
      y = var_label
    ) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey90"),
      strip.placement = "outside",
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
    ) +
    geom_text(
      data = sig_df,
      aes(x = 1.5, y = y_pos, label = sig),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      size = 4
    )
}

8.5 Effect size plots

build_diel_effect_df_one_scaled <- function(var_name, data = data_clean) {
  stopifnot(var_name %in% names(data))
  
  # scale the variable (global z-score)
  data_z <- data %>%
    mutate(var_z = as.numeric(scale(.data[[var_name]])))
  
  fml <- as.formula("var_z ~ Day_Night * Season * Benthos + (1|Quad_ID)")
  fit <- lmer(fml, data = data_z)
  
  # emmeans for Day_Night within each Season × Benthos
  emm <- emmeans(fit, ~ Day_Night | Season * Benthos)
  
  # Dusk - Dawn contrast in *scaled units* (≈ SD units)
  diel <- contrast(emm, method = "revpairwise")
  
  # summary with p-values + 95% CI
  df <- summary(diel, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE), level = 0.95) %>%
    as.data.frame()
  
  # standardize CI names
  if (!"lower.CL" %in% names(df)) {
    if ("asymp.LCL" %in% names(df)) {
      df <- df %>%
        rename(
          lower.CL = asymp.LCL,
          upper.CL = asymp.UCL
        )
    } else if ("LCL" %in% names(df)) {
      df <- df %>%
        rename(
          lower.CL = LCL,
          upper.CL = UCL
        )
    }
  }
  
  df %>%
    mutate(
      est_std   = estimate,     
      lower_std = lower.CL,
      upper_std = upper.CL,
      variable  = var_name
    )
}

## ANOVA

# filter out NAs
testing_df_norm <- testing_df_norm %>% 
  filter(!is.na(Value))%>%
  mutate(Season = as.factor(Season))

compute_sig_to_ctrl <- function(testing_df_norm, vars = numeric_vars_normal) {
  
  options(contrasts = c("contr.sum", "contr.poly")) # set contrasts for type III ANOVA
  
  res_tbl <- map(vars, function(v) {
    df <- testing_df_norm %>%
      filter(variable == v)
    
    fit <- lm(Value ~ Benthos * Day_Night * Season, data = df) # create lm
    model <- Anova(fit, type = "III")
    emm <- emmeans(fit, ~ Benthos | Day_Night * Season) # emmeans for tukey's hsd
    vs_ctrl <- contrast(emm, method = "trt.vs.ctrl", ref = control_label, adjust = "mvt")
    td  <- as.data.frame(vs_ctrl)
    
    comp_tbl <- td %>%
      separate(contrast, c("left","right"), sep = " - ", remove = FALSE) %>%
      mutate(
        Benthos  = if_else(right == control_label, left, right),
        variable = v,
        sig = case_when(
          is.na(p.value)  ~ NA_character_,
          p.value < 0.001 ~ "***",
          p.value < 0.01  ~ "**",
          p.value < 0.05  ~ "*",
          TRUE            ~ ""
        )
      ) 
    ctrl_tbl <- crossing(
      variable = v,
      Season   = unique(td$Season),
      Day_Night= unique(td$Day_Night),
      Benthos  = control_label
    ) %>%
      mutate(
        estimate = NA_real_, SE = NA_real_, df = NA_real_, t.ratio = NA_real_,
        p.value  = NA_real_, sig = ""
      )

    bind_rows(comp_tbl, ctrl_tbl) %>%
      distinct(variable, Season, Day_Night, Benthos, .keep_all = TRUE)
  }) %>% compact() %>% list_rbind()

  res_tbl
}

sig_to_ctrl <- compute_sig_to_ctrl(testing_df_norm) %>%
  mutate(variable = sub("_transformed$", "", variable)) # convert name back for join

9.1 One-sample t-test

compute_sig_to_ctrl_ttest <- function(testing_df_norm, 
                                      vars = numeric_vars_normal,
                                      control_label) {
  
  res_tbl <- map(vars, function(v) { # loop for each variable
    df_var <- testing_df_norm %>%
      filter(variable == v)
    
    res_by_sd <- df_var %>%
      group_nest(Season, Day_Night) %>% # group by season and dawn/dusk
      mutate(
        res = map(data, function(df_sd) {
          ctrl_vals <- df_sd %>%
            filter(Benthos == control_label) %>%
            pull(Value)
          ctrl_mean <- mean(ctrl_vals, na.rm = TRUE) # get OO mean

          df_sd %>%
            group_by(Benthos) %>%
            summarise(
              n       = sum(!is.na(Value)),
              mean    = mean(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
              .groups = "drop"
            ) %>%
            mutate(
              # one-sample test vs control mean for each benthos
              p.value = map_dbl(Benthos, function(b) {
                x <- df_sd %>% filter(Benthos == b) %>% pull(Value)
                t.test(x, mu = ctrl_mean)$p.value
              }),
              estimate = mean - ctrl_mean,
              variable = v
            )
        })
      ) %>%
      select(-data) %>%
      unnest(res)
    
    # add sig stars
    res_by_sd %>%
      mutate(
        sig = case_when(
          is.na(p.value)  ~ NA_character_,
          p.value < 0.001 ~ "***",
          p.value < 0.01  ~ "**",
          p.value < 0.05  ~ "*",
          TRUE            ~ ""
        )
      )
  }) %>% 
    compact() %>% 
    list_rbind()
  
  res_tbl
}

                                               vars = numeric_vars_normal,
                                               control_label = control_label) %>%
  mutate(variable = sub("_transformed$", "", variable))

9.2 Dunn’s test

compute_sig_to_ctrl_dunn <- function(testing_df_norm, 
                                     vars = numeric_vars,
                                     control_label) {
  
  res_tbl <- map(vars, function(v) { # loop for each variable
    df_var <- testing_df_norm %>%
      filter(variable == v)
    
    df_var %>%
      group_by(Season, Day_Night) %>% # group by season and dawn/dusk
      group_modify(~ {
        df_sd <- .x
  
        dunn_res <- df_sd %>%
          rstatix::dunn_test(Value ~ Benthos, p.adjust.method = "none")
        
        # keep only comparisons involving OO
        dunn_ctrl <- dunn_res %>%
          filter(group1 == control_label | group2 == control_label) %>%
          mutate(
            Benthos  = if_else(group1 == control_label, group2, group1),
            variable = v,
            p.value  = p.adj
          )
        
        dunn_ctrl
      }) %>%
      ungroup()
  }) %>%
    compact() %>%
    list_rbind() %>%
    mutate(
      sig = case_when(
        is.na(p.value)  ~ NA_character_,
        p.value < 0.001 ~ "***",
        p.value < 0.01  ~ "**",
        p.value < 0.05  ~ "*",
        TRUE            ~ ""
      )
    )
  
  res_tbl
}

  mutate(variable = sub("_transformed$", "", variable))

# lets look at all numeric vars just in case

# fall dusk = pH and humics
anovas_full_tidal_fall <- map_dfr(numeric_vars_normal, function(v){
  df_sub <- testing_df_norm %>%
    filter(variable == v,
           Season == "Fall",
          Day_Night == "Dusk")
    options(contrasts = c("contr.sum", "contr.poly"))
    fit <- lm(Value ~ Tide, data = df_sub)
    Anova(fit, type = "III") %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    rownames_to_column("term") %>%
    filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
    filter(`Pr(>F)` < 0.05) %>% # see what's significant
    mutate(variable = v)
})

# spring nothing
anovas_full_tidal_spring <- map_dfr(numeric_vars_normal, function(v){
  df_sub <- testing_df_norm %>%
    filter(variable == v,
           Season == "Spring",
          Day_Night == "Dawn")
    options(contrasts = c("contr.sum", "contr.poly"))
    fit <- lm(Value ~ Tide, data = df_sub)
    Anova(fit, type = "III") %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    rownames_to_column("term") %>%
    filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
    filter(`Pr(>F)` < 0.05) %>% # see what's significant
    mutate(variable = v)
})

11 Community Composition

11.1 Sessile

## sum across the canopy and understory ###

sessile_total <-sessile %>%
  group_by(plot, season)%>%
  summarise_at(.vars = vars(Silvetia_compressa:Chondracanthus_canaliculatus), .funs = sum)%>% 
  mutate(Total_hairs = rowSums(across(Silvetia_compressa:Chondracanthus_canaliculatus))) %>% # count total crosshairs
  ungroup()%>% # calculate percent cover
  mutate(across(c(Silvetia_compressa:Chondracanthus_canaliculatus),  ~ . /Total_hairs*100))%>%
  rename(BenthicID = plot, Season = season)%>% # keep consistent with other data
  mutate(Season = factor(Season, levels = c("summer2023","fall2023","winter2024", "spring2024")))%>%
  mutate(Benthos = case_when( # add benthos name
    grepl("B", BenthicID) ~ "Barnacles",
    grepl("M", BenthicID) ~"Mussels",
    grepl("P", BenthicID) ~"Surfgrass",
    grepl("R", BenthicID) ~"Rockweed"), 
    .after = BenthicID)


## Make a stacked barplot of all the species across seasons
sessile_total %>%
  group_by(Benthos, Season)%>% # calculate the average for each season
  summarise(across(c(Silvetia_compressa:Chondracanthus_canaliculatus),  ~mean(.,na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Silvetia_compressa:Chondracanthus_canaliculatus), names_to = "Species", values_to = "Percent_Cover")%>%
  left_join(sessile_function)%>%
  filter(Season %in% c('fall2023','spring2024')) %>%
  mutate(Season = factor(Season, 
    levels =  c("fall2023", "spring2024"), 
    labels = c("Fall", "Spring"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Season,y = Percent_Cover, fill = FunctionalGroup ))+
    geom_bar(position="stack", stat="identity")+
  scale_fill_paletteer_d("MetBrewer::Signac")+
  labs(x = "",
       y = "% Cover",
       color = "",
       fill = "Functional Group")+
  theme_bw()+
  facet_wrap(~Benthos)

#ggsave(here("Output","SessileComp.png"), width = 10, height = 6)

11.2 Mobiles

## calculate denisity per m2 (used 0.25m2 quad)
mobile_density <-
  mobile %>%
  rename(BenthicID = plot, Season = season)%>% # keep consistent with other data
  mutate(Season = factor(Season, levels = c("summer2023","fall2023","winter2024","spring2024")))%>%
  mutate(Benthos = case_when( # add benthos name
    grepl("B", BenthicID) ~ "Barnacles",
    grepl("M", BenthicID) ~"Mussels",
    grepl("P", BenthicID) ~"Surfgrass",
    grepl("R", BenthicID) ~"Rockweed"), 
    .after = BenthicID)%>%
  select(-c(Littorina_sp_raw, Lottia_sp_raw))%>%
  mutate(across(c(Lottia_sp_scaled:Strongylocentrotus_purpuratus),  ~./0.25))
  

mobile_density %>%
  group_by(Benthos, Season)%>% # calculate the average for each season
  summarise(across(c(Lottia_sp_scaled:Strongylocentrotus_purpuratus),  ~mean(.,na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Lottia_sp_scaled:Strongylocentrotus_purpuratus), names_to = "Species", values_to = "Density_m2")%>%
  left_join(mobile_function)%>% #join with functional data
  filter(Season %in% c('fall2023','spring2024')) %>%
  mutate(Season = factor(Season, 
    levels =  c("fall2023", "spring2024"), 
    labels = c("Fall", "Spring"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Season,y = Density_m2, fill = FunctionalGroup ))+
  geom_bar(position="stack", stat="identity")+
  scale_fill_paletteer_d("MetBrewer::Signac")+
  labs(x = "",
       y = expression(paste("Mean Density (m"^2,")")),
       color = "",
       fill = "Functional Group")+
  theme_bw()+
  facet_wrap(~Benthos, scale = "free")

## rename the foundation species data to match the chemistry
sessile_clean<-sessile_total %>%
  rename(Quad_ID = BenthicID) %>%
  mutate(Season = case_when(Season  == "fall2023"~"Fall",
                            Season == "spring2024"~"Spring",
                            Season == "summer2023"~"Summer",
                            Season == "winter2024"~"Winter")) %>%
  mutate(FoundationSp = case_when(Benthos == "Barnacles"~ `Balanus/Cthamalus_sp`,
                                   Benthos == "Rockweed"~Silvetia_compressa,
                                   Benthos == "Surfgrass"~Phyllospadix_sp,
                                   Benthos == "Mussels"~Mytilus_californianus)) %>%  # add a column that is the cover of the foundation species for the right benthos
  select(!Total_hairs) %>%
  mutate(Benthos = ifelse(Benthos == "Mussels","Mussel",Benthos))%>%
  mutate(Benthos = ifelse(Benthos == "Barnacles","Barnacle",Benthos))
